questions.prompt: An owner asks to give Finance the new app. What should be established before configuring grants?

options.text: Eligible population, resources/actions, timing, account rules, owners and removal expectations
options.explanation: A department label alone is not a complete access requirement.

options.text: Assign every Finance-related group immediately
options.explanation: Group names do not establish the approved population or permission scope.

options.text: Grant every user administrator access to avoid tickets
options.explanation: That broadens permissions beyond the request.

options.text: Copy the assignment and permissions from an app with a similar name
options.explanation: Similar branding does not establish the new application's approved population, permissions, matching or removal behavior.

review.heading: Turn the request into observable outcomes

questions.prompt: A proposed SAML connection supports SSO but no provisioning. What must the plan include?

options.text: A supported account creation, change and removal process with ownership
options.explanation: Sign-in federation does not by itself maintain target account lifecycle.

options.text: Assume SAML always provisions and deletes users
options.explanation: That is not an inherent property of the sign-in protocol.

options.text: Skip account readiness because SSO exists
options.explanation: The target still needs an eligible local identity relationship.

options.text: Use assignment as proof target removal is automatic
options.explanation: Assignment and downstream lifecycle outcomes differ.

review.heading: Translate the requirement without changing its meaning

questions.prompt: The identity team owns claims and the app team owns local roles. What should a design capture?

options.text: Which owner maintains and verifies each boundary and contract
options.explanation: Clear responsibility supports change, investigation and handover.

options.text: One team may silently redefine all rules
options.explanation: That removes controlled ownership and approval.

options.text: Only the vendor's public product name
options.explanation: A name does not identify local responsibilities.

options.text: No app owner is needed for federated access
options.explanation: The app still controls important local outcomes.

questions.prompt: An app needs employee ID and department but a proposal releases home address too. What should happen?

options.text: Release only justified attributes required by the integration
options.explanation: Unnecessary personal data adds exposure without serving the stated function.

options.text: Send every available profile field for future convenience
options.explanation: Availability is not a requirement to disclose data.

options.text: Encrypt it and stop assessing need
options.explanation: Confidentiality protection does not make unnecessary release necessary.

options.text: Move extra fields into navigation context instead
options.explanation: Relocating unnecessary information does not resolve the need question.

questions.prompt: A design proposes matching by display name because it is readable. What needs improvement?

options.text: An agreed unique, scoped identity key and supported matching behavior
options.explanation: Names can be duplicated or changed and are not sufficient by themselves.

options.text: Choose the most privileged account when names duplicate
options.explanation: Privilege is not ownership evidence.

options.text: Use any account with the same department
options.explanation: Department is not a unique identity key.

options.text: Ignore mapping because the assertion will be signed
options.explanation: A signature does not make every local lookup rule correct.

review.heading: Translate the requirement without changing its meaning

questions.prompt: Why include both allowed and denied cases in an access test plan?

options.text: To verify intended access and enforcement of boundaries
options.explanation: A positive baseline alone does not prove inappropriate access is rejected.

options.text: To remove restrictions until every case succeeds
options.explanation: Some test cases are supposed to be denied.

options.text: To replace target evidence with design assumptions
options.explanation: The actual receiver outcome must still be observed.

options.text: To prove every system shares one policy implementation
options.explanation: Different systems enforce different responsibilities.

review.heading: Make verification part of the requirement

questions.prompt: A change may block all app administrators. What should exist before activation?

options.text: An authorized, supported recovery route with owners, criteria and verification
options.explanation: Recovery should be concrete before the access-affecting change is applied.

options.text: Only a screenshot of a previous sign-in
options.explanation: Historical access is not a current recovery mechanism.

options.text: A plan to disable all validation automatically
options.explanation: Removing trust checks is not a sound default recovery strategy.

options.text: A promise that familiar products cannot lock out users
options.explanation: Product familiarity does not eliminate configuration risks.

review.heading: Plan recovery from an incorrect change

evidence: Primary administrator uses the same federated path
Authorized alternative recovery route: not yet verified

questions.prompt: An engineer plans to modify a policy shared by several apps. What is needed?

options.text: An impact assessment covering actual associations and relevant users
options.explanation: The visible ticket may be narrower than the shared configuration's effect.

options.text: Only a test for the app whose tab is open
options.explanation: That misses sibling app effects.

options.text: Only rename the policy to the requested app
options.explanation: Renaming does not change existing associations.

options.text: No recovery plan because the edit is small
options.explanation: A small edit can have large access consequences.

review.heading: Agree on who finishes each part

questions.prompt: A connection saves and an admin can open an app using an old local session. What remains untested?

options.text: Fresh federation, intended user/account mapping and the changed access requirements
options.explanation: Saved configuration and existing-session access can bypass the changed path.

options.text: Whether the settings page accepted the save
options.explanation: That observed state is already supplied.

options.text: Whether the admin can use that existing session
options.explanation: That limited access was directly observed.

options.text: Whether every normal user must be an administrator
options.explanation: That is not a consequence of connection testing.

review.heading: Make verification part of the requirement

questions.prompt: Which handover best supports ongoing engineering work?

options.text: Environment, authoritative values, owners, test evidence, limitations and recovery steps
options.explanation: Another engineer needs the actual contract and verified state, not just a success claim.

options.text: Only the phrase SSO works
options.explanation: That leaves scope and evidence unclear.

options.text: Only private credentials in an unprotected note
options.explanation: Secrets are not a substitute for a maintained operational agreement.

options.text: Only an unlabeled XML example
options.explanation: Without context it cannot establish the intended environment or behavior.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
evidence: Handover identifies environment, approved values and owners
Controlled test results and limitations are recorded
Recovery criteria and procedure are included

questions.prompt: A required removal behavior is unsupported by the target connector. What should release planning do?

options.text: Make the gap explicit and obtain an approved supported alternative before claiming readiness
options.explanation: Unsupported automation does not establish the required business outcome.

options.text: Mark it complete because the sign-in test passed
options.explanation: Sign-in success does not verify removal.

options.text: Assume a future feature already provides it
options.explanation: A proposal is not current capability or evidence.

options.text: Delete the requirement from the record silently
options.explanation: That hides an unresolved obligation rather than resolving it.

review.heading: Agree on who finishes each part

evidence: Business removal requirement: immediate target termination
Connector: does not support that requested operation
Approved alternative and owner: not yet established

questions.prompt: After a change, which result supports closing the specific issue?

options.text: A fresh controlled test exercises the corrected boundary and confirms intended access and rejection
options.explanation: Closure needs observed behavior against the agreed requirement.

options.text: Only the approved change ticket
options.explanation: Approval does not prove execution or effect.

options.text: Only a preview of a proposed value
options.explanation: Preview does not prove target state.

options.text: Only an unrelated successful request
options.explanation: Different operation evidence does not verify this correction.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

review.heading: Make verification part of the requirement
